findings.description: The boot server -> machines return arrow is visible, but its required boot.ipxe + S3 args payload is absent from every v2 diagram state. The final spec also abbreviates away args. Recorded final --check and validator confirm one skipped caption; neither the warning nor the spec supplies visible label proof.

diagnose uploads [25,34,16,1] sits flush against machines -> S3 at (24,34), while River -> S3 turns at (22,34) on the other side of that route. It reads as a second machines -> S3 caption, defeating the explicit separate jobs-diagnostics relation. Intended ownership in JSON does not resolve the visible misattachment.

audit + reimage [25,17,15,1] loses verify from audit / verify reimage. Reimage is not an abbreviation for verify reimage: it reads as an operation instead of verification. Its most plausible owner is the River -> SSH arrow, but the payload is changed even after resolving that weaker ownership ambiguity.

The full-label fit gate fails because the boot response caption is omitted, despite ample unclipped grid and complete visible boxes. This is label-placement loss, not cropping at a viewport boundary. A correctly sized capture cannot rescue absent required text.

Across 0/100/200/300/400ms, dots remain at e2 (20,8), e4 (21,16), e5 (20,24), and e7 (17,40). The supplied required motion sequence shows static markers on four requested animated lines. flow:0.5 and dots:1 are not proof of live movement.

Direction/cadence remains unproven on four two-position sequences: e6 (19,32)<->(18,33); e12 (24,32)<->(25,33); e15 (24,14)<->(24,15); e20 (46,23)<->(46,24). Samples may reflect legitimate short-cycle wrapping, but they cannot establish forward live travel without assumptions. This is an evidence blocker, not a proven reverse-motion defect.

blockers: Renderer label-placement gap in the executed v2 tb boot-response return route: payload caption is missing. Archived two-node tb checks, including a shorter reverse label, each report 1/2 labels, while the archived lr check reports 2/2. This supports a local upward-tb label-slot defect, not universal inability to render the exchange; lr is a recorded possible workaround, not a validated replacement final view.

Required per-route motion proof remains incomplete: four routes are visibly stationary in the supplied sequence, four show only two-position alternation. Longer/non-aliased captures and usable visible travel on short routes are required; dots:1/flow:0.5 cannot remove this blocker. The evidence does not establish a universal renderer animation incapability.
